title: 2 Core concepts
body:
2 Core concepts
Four ideas explain the whole plugin.

Transcripts: how a page becomes text
A page of handwriting is an image. To search it, quote it, or discuss it, it has to become text. That is what READ
does, and every page goes through the same two steps:
STEP 1 · OCR

STEP 2 · VISION

Mistral OCR 4 reads the page

Ministral 14B reads the image

Fast, cheap and powerful. It returns the text plus a

With the OCR text riding along as a hint. Vision

confidence score for each word, but it doesn't

understands layout, tables, drawings, margin

“see” drawings, schemas or handwritten notes on

notes and your own conventions, and it follows the

a PDF, and takes no instructions.

prompt you can edit (§3.3).

Each result is stored on the tablet with a fingerprint of the page. Change the ink and only that page is re-read;
never touch it and it is never paid for twice. The fingerprint follows the content, not the location: move a note or
PDF to another folder, or move or copy a page between two notes, and its transcript is found again, never
re-charged. PDFs differ: the whole file is read in one OCR call, then each page gets a Vision pass, so annotations
and figures are read too. Low-confidence words come back underlined, tap to correct; a hand-corrected page is
marked as yours and never overwritten.
Page after page, those transcripts become a library: your own local, searchable copy of what you wrote. It powers
Search (one query across every notebook, in seconds) and Export. Nothing is uploaded to build it, it lives in the
plugin's private storage, on the device only.

Chat and agents
Once a page has a transcript (or on demand, live), you can chat about it. The floating assistant is a movable panel
that sits over your note. It always knows what you are looking at, and you can add anything else: other pages,
whole notebooks, a lassoed image.
An agent is the same chat with a memory of its own: a name, a persona, a model, and a set of library documents it
always knows. Four ready-made agents ship with the plugin and can be added in one tap:
Extractor: actions, dates, figures

Writer: notes into clean prose

Tutor: explains & quizzes you

Brainstorm: pushes ideas further

They are ordinary agents once added: rename them, change their model, give them documents. And you create
your own, a “Meeting notes” agent over your work notebooks, a “Recipes” agent, a “Thesis” agent that knows a
long PDF and quotes it. You pick one when you start a conversation.

The menu: one button, everything behind it
The Supernote toolbar entry SmartNote AI Menu opens a compact menu over your page.

3.3 · Configuration Door 2: READ: AI transcript params
This door shapes what the AI is told when it reads a page. It drives the Vision step.

Fig. 3.2, Prompt blocks.

Fig. 3.3, Glossary & helpers.

The prompt is not hidden: it is a list of editable blocks, joined into the instruction actually sent. The shipped blocks
are a tested, high-performing base, but they are tuned to my notes: to get good results on yours, you must
adapt them to your own context, the language(s) you write in, your names, acronyms and jargon (the Glossary),
your financial and unit conventions, and how you use drawings and templates. Every block has a Reset, plus a
Reset to default, all this page at the top, so you can experiment freely.

title: Web search is one-shot: you arm it in the chat panel and it applies to your next
body:
Web search is one-shot: you arm it in the chat panel and it applies to your next message only. Web answers
cite their sources (~0.01 € per search).
Answer style. Precise sticks to the facts, Creative allows looser phrasing, Balanced is the model's own tuning.
Persona (system prompt). Who the assistant is and how it talks to you, prepended to every conversation.
Quick actions are the one-tap prompts under the chat input. Toggle, reorder, edit or add your own; they write
into the input field so you can adapt before sending. Lasso quick actions (up to 3) appear only while a
lassoed image is in context.
Context documents & cost. Build an agent's context from the Library. Folders and whole notes stay live
(future pages included automatically); specific pages are fixed. The screen tells you how many pages are
already read, what reading the rest would cost, and the token weight, less context is cheaper. Within a
conversation only the first message pays the full context; caching then bills the rest at about 10%.

4.1 · Synchronisation
Every folder and note carries a mode chip, set with one tap. Setting a chip costs nothing, it only saves a
preference. A folder's mode covers everything under it; a single document can override its folder. A row that follows
its parent shows an inherited chip, ↳ Sync: X (the mode it takes from above); tapping cycles Off → Manual → Auto
→ inherit when a parent folder is tracked, so you can always fall back to the folder's choice.

A good habit: active notebooks on Auto, archives on Manual, anything private on Off.

What actually triggers an Auto read
Auto is not a system service, it is the plugin working while it is alive.
What is read. Only pages whose content actually changed since their last read; the page under your pen is left
alone. Writing sends nothing. The append-only .note format lets the plugin compare, for free, file size, then page
fingerprints, then each page's revision. An unchanged page is never sent again, and a page that merely moved
(renamed folder, or copied into another note) keeps its transcript and is not paid for twice.
When the plugin looks. Ordinary moments trigger a check, pen-lift or page turn, the assistant's pulse, returning
to the plugin or opening the Library/config, every 15 min as a fallback, at start-up, and after an unfinished
backlog pass.

title: Checks are throttled to one every 20 s, and most cost nothing. The page under yo
body:
Checks are throttled to one every 20 s, and most cost nothing. The page under your pen is read only when needed
and never while you're on it (its render would be blank), in practice when you turn away or open the Library, and
never more than once a minute. Asking about the page you just wrote works: when you send a message, the
assistant reads anything out of date in your context, current page included, before answering.

Notes and PDFs have different constraints
A page is rendered by the app that owns it: note pages need the note app in the background; PDF Vision needs the
document reader. The OCR step of a PDF is the exception, it reads the file's bytes whatever is on screen. The
plugin probes what it can render at every pass (Rendering via: note app / PDF reader / none yet). If PDF Vision
pages wait and rendering fails, a ▶ Resume PDF Vision button appears, you decide when to tap it; the plugin
never opens a document by itself.

HONEST LIMITS
Auto works while the plugin lives. Close
everything and it pauses, then resumes where
it stopped.
In the background, how long the system keeps it
running is out of the plugin's hands.
Nothing runs while the device is off.

Fig. 4.2, The Synchronisation frame.

A page takes roughly 8-30 s (render + OCR +
Vision). A first full-notebook sync is a “start it and
let it run” job.
Unsupervised, Auto reads at most 500 pages
per session; actions you ask for yourself
(Sync now, Force sync, Force Vision) have no
such cap.

The panel. AUTO: last sync, pending count, Force sync. MANUAL: last sync, pending count with price, Sync now,
and Check changes (free re-scan); when a manual pass is queued it shows the standing Sync order with a ✕
Cancel to drop it. SYNC STATUS: a progress bar split by type, with details: 1. Queue · 2. OCR done, Vision to do
(▶ Force Vision) · 3. Finished. A ⏹ Stop button interrupts any pass; paid pages are kept.

title: 4.2 · Browse transcripts
body:
4.2 · Browse transcripts

Fig. 4.3, Pages as tiles.

Fig. 4.4, One page, three views.

Open a document to see every page as a tile: the first lines of its transcript, its source, or not read yet. A page read
and found empty says (blank page), it is done, not pending. Open a page and you get three things side by side: the
transcript, the original page image, and the Supernote's own live OCR (free, for comparison).
From here you can: edit the transcript by hand (a corrected page is marked as yours and never overwritten); tap
an underlined “unsure” word to fix just that word; Redo AI transcript to re-read the page (a single unified OCR +
Vision pass); Rotate right + redo or Rotate left + redo to re-read a page rotated 90° (rarely needed, landscape
pages are usually straightened automatically); and Export this page or add it to the chat.

Lock a page or a document
A lock freezes a transcript you are happy with. Lock a single page from its page view, or a whole document from
the page grid, whose chip then reads

🔒 Lock document (N p. locked); locked rows also show a 🔒 in the

Library. A locked page is never re-read automatically, even if its ink changes later, so a page you have handcorrected stays exactly as you left it. On a locked page the Redo AI transcript and Rotate right / left + redo
buttons are greyed out and decline; the lock/unlock toggle and Edit stay available, so manual corrections are
always allowed.
The lock survives sync and Restore backup, and it blocks every Clear: a locked document refuses its own Clear,
and locked pages survive a document Clear, Clear transcripts of Off notes and Clear ALL transcripts alike. The
confirmation message spells out what will be kept.

4.3 · Search
Search runs over your local transcripts only, what has already
been read. An Off document, or one never synced, is invisible
until you sync it. Results are capped, and the line under the
field always shows how your query was understood. On each
result line you can open the transcript, Go to page (the
Supernote opens the real page), or add the page to the chat.

Fig. 4.5, Search.

title: 5 The floating assistant
body:
5 The floating assistant
Open the assistant gives you a movable, resizable
panel that floats over your note: you keep writing on
the page while you talk about it.
Drag the header to move it, the black bar at the bottom to
resize, the ⌄ button to collapse it into a floating bubble, ⛶ to
snap it to a corner or full screen, and ✕ to close it.

Fig. 5.1, The floating panel.

5.1 · CHAT
The brain dropdown (name + arrow in the header) switches between CHAT and your agents. It shows the current
model, how many documents and pages are loaded, New chat, and your History.
Quick actions under the input write a prompt into the field; you send it yourself with the M button.
Web is one-shot: arm it and it applies to the next message only. Web answers cite their sources.
A Stop button is always available while the assistant works.
Reading pages not read yet starts right away; only a large batch (more than 100 pages) asks you to confirm the
price first. Below that, the read begins directly and its cost shows in the Library's MANUAL panel. Off files ask for a
one-time consent, and their text is stored nowhere.
Follow-up questions cost about 10% of the first, thanks to prompt caching.

5.2 · Agents
Pick an agent from the brain dropdown when you start a
conversation. It brings its persona, model, answer style,
quick actions and its documents. You can also change
agent mid-conversation to change the chat's behaviour,
the full history is sent to the new model, so the
discussion continues.

Fig. 5.2, The brain dropdown.

5.5 · Lasso
Select part of a page with the Supernote lasso and tap Ask SmartNote AI. The selection is attached to the
conversation as an image, it rides on whatever chat or agent is active. The image stays as a Lasso chip until you
remove it (add several if you want). The instruction sent with it is the Lasso: image reading directive (Door 2),
editable or empty. Your lasso quick actions (Door 3) appear while an image is in context. No transcription is
involved: lasso a diagram and ask “explain this”, lasso a to-do and ask “turn this into a checklist”.

6.2 · Why Mistral only
Why Mistral, and why Mistral only? That is a deliberate choice, here is the reasoning.

title: Our handwritten notes are among the most personal data we own, and privacy was m
body:
Our handwritten notes are among the most personal data we own, and privacy was my key concern throughout this
plugin's development. The question is not only “is the model smart?” but “under whose laws does this text land,
and who can compel access to it?”
The plugin already keeps exposure small: everything stays on the tablet, each request is transient (no memory
beyond a short-lived cache), and Off files are never sent. But the biggest privacy factor is the choice of AI provider.

Mistral · EU (France)

Other jurisdictions

All API requests fall under the GDPR: no training

In the US, the CLOUD Act lets authorities compel

on your data on a paid plan, use limited to

a US company to hand over data wherever it is

answering your request, real security duties, and

stored, and FISA §702 targets surveillance of non-

enforceable rights (access, deletion) with

US persons abroad. In China, the National

regulators and heavy fines behind them, a legal

Intelligence Law (Art. 7) and the Data Security

framework that has demonstrated its strength, not

Law require companies to cooperate with the

a settings toggle.

state on request. A training opt-out only helps as
far as you trust it is honoured.

In the US or China? An EU model may help you too: your notes get European-grade handling and sit outside your
own country's easiest reach. No provider hides you from a determined state, and nothing dangerous should go into
any cloud, but for everyday notes, moving them under EU law is a real gain wherever you live.
Is the quality there? For reading your handwriting and answering about your own pages, what matters is legibility
and your glossary, not frontier reasoning, and Mistral's OCR and vision models are strong at exactly that (chosen
on measured results, not on brand). Top providers are clearly ahead in raw capability, but Mistral is “good enough”
for Supernote needs, and that trade-off is made on purpose, driven by privacy first.

body:
The name and logo are not covered by the licence: “SmartNote AI” and its icon stay mine, a fork must ship under its
own name.

Why AGPL: the code is open for anyone to inspect, which matters for a plugin that handles your notes and claims
to protect your privacy, but nobody can take the work, swap a few pieces, and close it up as their own product. The
full licence text ships with the sources (LICENSE).
